newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenia parliament lifts opposition MPs' immunity.
newsitem.headline: Armenia parliament lifts opposition MPs' immunity.

text.p: Armenia's parliament voted on Thursday to lift the immunity of eight opposition deputies, including defeated presidential challenger Vazgen Manukyan, to allow prosecutors to press criminal charges against them.

A prosecutor accused the opposition deputies of trying to organise a coup and take power through violence which endangered peoples' lives. He was referring to violent clashes between Manukyan's supporters and riot police on Wednesday. Parliamentary deputies are usually immune from prosecution.
Opposition deputy Shalash Kocharyan dismissed allegations of an attempted coup as "fiction", but parliament nevertheless voted 155-0 with two abstentions to lift Manukyan's immunity.
Manukyan, a former prime minister, was not present, but the other seven deputies were led out of the hall by armed soldiers.
Manukyan's supporters have accused Ter-Petrosyan's camp of rigging Sunday's presidential election and said that, contrary to the official result, Manukyan had won.

Thursday's clampdown on the opposition brought troops and ligght tanks into the streets of Yerevan. It followed clashes between thousands of Manukyan's supporters and riot police on Wednesday in which one person was said to have been killed.
